reported_symptom: System fails to boot with a black screen and Caps Lock LED blinking 2 long and 2 short flashes after a BIOS update initiated via Windows Update or HP Support Assistant.
root_cause_analysis: BIOS flash write to the 9 MB System BIOS SPI ROM was interrupted because the update was triggered while docked or running on battery power instead of direct AC power.
resolution_steps: 1) Disconnect all external docks/peripherals and connect the 65W USB-C AC adapter (L04650-850) directly (Manual p.81). 2) Hold the power button for 15 seconds to force shutdown, then power on and allow HP Sure Start (8 MB isolated flash) to automatically restore the Golden BIOS image. 3) If automatic recovery does not trigger, hold Win+B while pressing Power for 3 seconds to invoke BIOS Recovery and re-flash sp148210.

reported_symptom: External dual 4K monitors intermittently flicker or go blank and 2.5GbE Ethernet drops out when resuming from sleep while connected to the HP Thunderbolt 120W G4 Dock (M97105-001).
root_cause_analysis: Link training timeout between the host Intel Maple Ridge Thunderbolt 4 retimer and the G4 Dock DisplayPort MST hub during Windows 11 Modern Standby (S0ix) resume.
resolution_steps: 1) Install the latest HP Thunderbolt Dock G4 firmware package (sp149503) and System BIOS (sp148210). 2) Unplug the AC power cord from the dock for 30 seconds to clear the dock DMC cache. 3) Verify Thunderbolt security and PCIe power management states in F10 Computer Setup.

reported_symptom: Red X appears on the Windows system tray speaker icon after a Windows 11 cumulative update; both the Bang & Olufsen quad speakers and internal array microphones disappear from sound settings.
root_cause_analysis: Windows Update overwrote the HP-customized Intel Smart Sound Technology (Intel SST) OED driver with a generic build, causing DSP audio pipeline initialization failure (Device Manager Error Code 10).
resolution_steps: 1) Open Device Manager -> System Devices and inspect 'Intel Smart Sound Technology OED' and 'Audio Controller'. 2) Roll back the driver or install the official HP Intel SST + Realtek HD Audio package (sp146831). 3) Inspect the 3.5mm audio jack (N31280-001) for debris causing false headset detection (internal speakers are automatically disabled when a jack plug is sensed per Manual p.6).

reported_symptom: Laptop becomes hot inside a carrying bag with the lid closed and drains the battery to 0% within a few hours, causing the left-side battery light to blink amber rapidly.
root_cause_analysis: Windows Modern Standby (S0 Low Power Idle) network/Bluetooth wake events or slight flex of the folio cover inside a tight bag triggering the Hall sensor to wake the CPU in an enclosed space.
resolution_steps: 1) Run `powercfg /sleepstudy` in an elevated prompt to identify offending Modern Standby wake sources. 2) Update BIOS to sp148210 and configure the lid-close action on battery to 'Hibernate' before placing the notebook in a bag. 3) Run F2 UEFI Battery Diagnostics and replace the 4-cell 53 Whr battery (M90788-005) if cell degradation is reported.

reported_symptom: The 8 MP IR webcam shows a black feed in Zoom/Teams or fails to detect presence, while the keyboard camera key light remains illuminated.
root_cause_analysis: Either the electronic HP Camera Privacy Key on the top-right of the keyboard is toggled ON (LED On = Camera Off per Table 2-5 p.10), or repeated pull-forward folio hinge articulation loosened the camera ZIF cable on the Display Hub Board (N22937-001).
resolution_steps: 1) Press the HP Camera Privacy Key on the keyboard row until the camera key LED turns OFF (LED Off = Camera On). 2) Check F10 Computer Setup -> Built-in Device Options to confirm Integrated Camera is enabled. 3) If USB/MIPI enumeration still fails, remove the display panel (8 pull-tab adhesive strips) and reseat or replace the 8 MP Camera Module (N23306-001) and Display Hub Board ZIF cables (Manual p.56-68).

reported_symptom: Intel 5000 5G WWAN module (N00181-005) drops cellular connection under heavy data transfer, or system halts at POST with 'Unauthorized Wireless Module Detected' after a field WWAN swap.
root_cause_analysis: 1) Thermal throttling of the 5G modem if the two captive screws on the right fan of the Heat Sink (N22936-001) were not re-tightened over the WWAN thermal pad extension. 2) BIOS FCC whitelist blocks non-HP spare part WWAN cards.
resolution_steps: 1) Install only official HP-authorized WWAN spare parts (5G: N00181-005 or LTE: N00182-005 per Manual p.39). 2) Verify the thermal pad under the right section of Heat Sink (N22936-001) contacts the WWAN module and tighten both right-fan captive screws (Manual p.40-41). 3) Update 5G modem firmware via sp147415.

reported_symptom: HP Dragonfly Folio Digital Pen (N02954-001) does not charge wirelessly when attached to the right-side magnetic pen slot.
root_cause_analysis: Loose upper or lower ZIF ribbon cable on the internal Wireless Charging Module (N26149-001) or mechanical misalignment of the Magnetic Pen Slot holder (N26148-001).
resolution_steps: 1) Confirm the pen is seated squarely in the right-side magnetic attachment and charging area (Table 2-1 p.5). 2) Remove the bottom cover (N22918-001) and disconnect the battery (M90788-005). 3) Reseat the top and bottom ZIF connectors on the Wireless Charging Module (N26149-001) or replace the module using Cable Kit N22929-001 (Manual p.41-42; cannot be removed from outside).

reported_symptom: Dual cooling fans spin loudly and the upper keyboard deck becomes warm during video conferencing and multi-tab browser workloads.
root_cause_analysis: Aggressive Intel 12th Gen Alder Lake short-duration turbo boost (PL2) power spikes combined with obstructed side/bottom air vents on soft surfaces or degraded thermal paste on the heat sink.
resolution_steps: 1) Open HP Command Center / MyHP and switch thermal profile from 'Performance' to 'Cool' or 'Quiet'. 2) Operate the notebook only on a hard, flat surface so left, right, and bottom air vents remain unobstructed (Manual Safety Warning p.iii & p.5-6). 3) If overheating persists, remove Heat Sink (N22936-001), clean old thermal grease, and apply fresh thermal compound (Manual p.47-48).

reported_symptom: Physical keyboard, function keys, and power button remain completely unresponsive after returning the pull-forward display from tablet/media mode back to laptop mode.
root_cause_analysis: By design, the keyboard, function keys, and power key are disabled in stand, tent, and tablet modes (Manual p.8 NOTE). If the bottom edge of the display is not seated into the clamshell magnetic groove, the Hall/IMU sensors keep the keyboard locked.
resolution_steps: 1) Return the display fully into standard Clamshell mode so the bottom display edge engages the keyboard deck sensor. 2) Close and reopen the lid once to re-trigger the Hall sensor. 3) If stuck in tablet mode continuously, inspect the Display Cable Kit (N22930-001) and eCompass/Hall sensor connections on the Display Hub Board (N22937-001).

reported_symptom: System fails to POST with a blank screen while Caps Lock LED blinks 3 long flashes followed by 2 short flashes.
root_cause_analysis: Hardware initialization failure on the onboard soldered LPDDR5-6400 memory modules. Because RAM is soldered directly to the motherboard and non-upgradeable, individual DIMM replacement is impossible.
resolution_steps: 1) Unplug AC power and hold the power button for 15-30 seconds to perform an RTC/EC hard reset. 2) If the 3-long, 2-short Caps Lock blink persists, replace the entire System Board (e.g., N20720-601 or N20728-601) following the Prerequisite Removal sequence: Bottom Cover -> Battery -> Heat Sink -> 10 Board Cables -> System Board (Manual p.50-53).

reported_symptom: Notebook displays 'No Bootable Device Found' and F2 HP PC Hardware Diagnostics UEFI Storage Test fails with a 24-digit Hardware Failure ID code.
root_cause_analysis: Controller or TLC NAND sector failure on the M.2 2280 PCIe Gen4x4 NVMe SSD (M52027-005).
resolution_steps: 1) Record the 24-digit failure ID or scan the QR code in UEFI Diagnostics to log an HP EAS warranty replacement (Manual p.84-86). 2) Remove Bottom Cover (N22918-001) and disconnect Battery (M90788-005). 3) Remove the Phillips M1.4x1.2 screw, slide off the Mylar sleeve, transfer the double-sided Mylar shield to the replacement SSD (M52027-005), and restore the OS via HP Sure Recover (F9) or HP Cloud Recovery USB (Manual p.35-36, p.77-79).

reported_symptom: After installing Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or Fedora on Elite Dragonfly G3, Wi-Fi 6E (AX211) works but the top two speakers produce no sound and the 5MP/8MP MIPI camera is not detected.
root_cause_analysis: Older Linux kernels lack the Alder Lake Sound Open Firmware (SOF) discrete smart-amplifier topology quirk and Intel IPU6 MIPI camera out-of-tree drivers.
resolution_steps: 1) Upgrade to Linux kernel 6.2+ and `sof-firmware` 2.2.4+ to enable all four Bang & Olufsen discrete speaker amplifiers. 2) Flash the latest HP System BIOS (sp148210) to apply updated ACPI DSDT audio pin configuration tables.
